# Game of Thrones: character, relationship, event and battle reference

**Full spoilers for the HBO television series, Seasons 1–8.** Researched 11 October 2026.

This guide covers the main cast, recurring characters, many named guest characters, distinct unnamed plot roles, flashback figures, dragons and direwolves. It is a broad reference, not a certified inventory of every credited extra. Some minor characters have only a single scene and no established later history. Their missing biographies are left unknown rather than invented. Characters mentioned only in dialogue are separated from characters who actually appear.

**Reading the timelines:** S3 means Season 3; S3E9 means Season 3, Episode 9. A season range marks the relevant story period and does not mean the character appears in every intervening season. Flashbacks, visions and corpses are identified when relevant. The show does not provide a dependable calendar for every event, so episode order is more useful than assigning speculative years.

**Sources and canon:** Linked character articles include both book and TV material; this guide uses their television accounts. Episode articles are used for event order and outcomes. The [television cast index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Game_of_Thrones_characters) is a navigation aid, not proof that every minor figure has a complete biography. Fan-wiki dates and inferred off-screen deaths are not automatically treated as established screen facts.

## 1. The relationships that explain the story

| Family or alliance | Relationship and significance |
|---|---|
| Stark household | Ned and Catelyn are parents of Robb, Sansa, Arya, Bran and Rickon. Jon is raised as their half-brother but is actually their first cousin. Theon grows up among them as Ned's ward and political hostage. |
| Jon's true family | Rhaegar Targaryen and Lyanna Stark are Jon's parents. Ned is his maternal uncle; Daenerys is his paternal aunt. Jon and Daenerys become lovers before learning this. |
| Lannister household | Tywin is father to twins Jaime and Cersei and their younger brother Tyrion. Jaime and Cersei's incestuous relationship produces Joffrey, Myrcella and Tommen, publicly presented as Robert's children. |
| Baratheon succession | Robert, Stannis and Renly are brothers. Once Cersei's children's parentage is exposed, Stannis claims the throne as Robert's legitimate heir; Renly competes despite being younger. Gendry is Robert's biological son. |
| Tully–Arryn connection | Catelyn, Lysa and Edmure are siblings. Lysa marries Jon Arryn and has Robin; later she marries Littlefinger. Brynden Tully is their uncle. |
| Tyrell connection | Olenna is Mace's mother; Mace is father to Margaery and Loras. Loras loves Renly. Margaery successively marries Renly, Joffrey and Tommen. |
| Greyjoy connection | Balon is father to Yara and Theon. Euron and Aeron are Balon's brothers. Euron seizes power from this family and allies with Cersei. |
| Martell connection | Doran, Oberyn and Elia are siblings. Trystane is Doran's son; Ellaria is Oberyn's partner. Obara, Nymeria and Tyene are Oberyn's daughters; of these three, Tyene is also Ellaria's daughter. |
| Mormont connection | Jeor is Jorah's father. Lyanna Mormont is the daughter of Jeor's sister Maege, making Jorah and Lyanna first cousins. |

The Stark and Targaryen connections are established through [Ned's history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ned_Stark) and [Jon's television storyline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Snow_(character)); the royal parentage is central to [Cersei's storyline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cersei_Lannister). The later revelation is shown in [S7E7, “The Dragon and the Wolf”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dragon_and_the_Wolf).

## 2. The Starks and their closest companions

| Character | Relationships, highlights and timeline |
|---|---|
| **Eddard “Ned” Stark** | Catelyn's husband, Robert's friend and Jon's secret uncle. S1: becomes Hand, discovers the royal children's parentage, is betrayed by Littlefinger and executed on Joffrey's orders in S1E9. S6–7 flashbacks reveal his protection of Jon. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ned_Stark) |
| **Catelyn Stark** | Born a Tully; mother of five Stark children. S1: captures Tyrion, helping escalate hostilities. S2: releases Jaime in hopes of retrieving her daughters. S3E9: murdered at the Red Wedding with Robb. The television series never resurrects her as Lady Stoneheart. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catelyn_Stark) |
| **Robb Stark** | Eldest Stark son; Theon's close friend; Talisa's husband. S1: wins victories and becomes King in the North. S2–3: marriage to Talisa breaks his Frey promise; executing Rickard Karstark weakens his army. Roose murders him at the Red Wedding. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robb_Stark) |
| **Sansa Stark** | Joffrey's former betrothed; married to Tyrion, then Ramsay. S1–3: royal hostage. S4: escapes with Littlefinger. S5: abused by Ramsay and escapes with Theon. S6: helps regain Winterfell; S7: condemns Littlefinger; S8: becomes queen of an independent North. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sansa_Stark) |
| **Arya Stark** | Jon's especially close cousin; student of Syrio and the Faceless Men; companion of the Hound and Gendry. S1–4: escapes and survives the Riverlands. S5–6: trains in Braavos. S6–7: takes revenge on the Freys. S8: kills the Night King and sails west. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arya_Stark) |
| **Brandon “Bran” Stark** | Ned's younger son; protected by Hodor, Osha and the Reeds. S1: Jaime's attack leaves him unable to walk. S3–4: travels north. S6: succeeds the Three-Eyed Raven. S7–8: reveals hidden history and helps lure the Night King; elected king of six kingdoms. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bran_Stark) |
| **Rickon Stark** | Youngest Stark child; Osha protects him after Winterfell falls. Leaves Bran's group in S3. S6: the Umbers deliver him to Ramsay, who kills him immediately before the Battle of the Bastards. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rickon_Stark) |
| **Jon Snow / Aegon Targaryen** | Raised as Ned's illegitimate son; actually Rhaegar and Lyanna's son. S1–4: joins the Watch, loves Ygritte and defends the Wall. S5–6: elected commander, murdered, resurrected and becomes northern king. S7–8: allies with and loves Daenerys, then kills her after her massacre; exiled and last seen going beyond the Wall. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Snow_(character)) |
| **Benjen Stark** | Ned and Lyanna's brother, Jon's uncle and Watch ranger. Vanishes in S1; returns in S6, explaining that the Children prevented his transformation into a wight. Saves Bran and Meera, then sacrifices himself saving Jon in S7E6. |
| **Hodor / Wylis** | Winterfell stablehand who carries Bran. S1–6: loyal protector. S6E5 reveals that Bran's contact across time causes young Wylis's catastrophic experience of his future death. Dies holding a door against wights so Bran and Meera can escape. |
| **Osha** | Wildling captured in S1 who becomes Bran and Rickon's protector. Helps them escape Theon in S2; takes Rickon away in S3. Ramsay kills her during an attempted attack on him in S6. |
| **Jojen Reed** | Howland's son and Meera's brother; has prophetic dreams. S3–4: guides Bran toward the Three-Eyed Raven. Fatally wounded outside the cave in S4E10; Meera ends his suffering. |
| **Meera Reed** | Jojen's sister; Bran's principal physical protector after Hodor dies. S3–7: brings Bran north and home again. Leaves Winterfell to return to her family; subsequent fate is not shown. |
| **Talisa Maegyr / Stark** | Volantene healer who meets Robb during his campaign in S2. Their marriage undermines the Frey alliance. She and their unborn child are murdered at the Red Wedding in S3E9. |

For the companions' critical turning points, see [“The Children”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Children_(Game_of_Thrones)), [“The Door”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Door_(Game_of_Thrones)), [Rickon's television story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rickon_Stark) and [“Beyond the Wall”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond_the_Wall_(Game_of_Thrones)). Talisa's fate is documented in [“The Rains of Castamere”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rains_of_Castamere).

## 3. The Lannisters, the royal children and their allies

| Character | Relationships, highlights and timeline |
|---|---|
| **Tyrion Lannister** | Tywin's youngest child; Jaime's beloved brother and Cersei's enemy; Shae's lover and Sansa's husband. S2: organizes Blackwater's defense. S4: falsely tried for Joffrey's murder; kills Shae and Tywin. S5–8: advises Daenerys, rejects her massacre and becomes Bran's Hand. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrion_Lannister) |
| **Cersei Lannister** | Robert's wife; Jaime's twin and lover; mother of three royal children. S1–4: protects their dynasty. S5: empowers the Faith, which imprisons her. S6: destroys the Great Sept and becomes queen. S7–8: allies with Euron, refuses the northern war; dies with Jaime beneath the Red Keep. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cersei_Lannister) |
| **Jaime Lannister** | Kingsguard knight, Tyrion's protector, Cersei's lover and later Brienne's lover. S1: pushes Bran. S2–3: captivity, loss of his hand and bond with Brienne expose a more complex man. S8: fights for the living, knights Brienne, returns to Cersei and dies with her. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaime_Lannister) |
| **Tywin Lannister** | Father of Jaime, Cersei and Tyrion; architect of Lannister supremacy. S1–3: campaigns against Robb, wins with the Tyrell alliance and supports the Red Wedding plot. S4: presides over Tyrion's trial; Tyrion kills him in S4E10. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tywin_Lannister) |
| **Joffrey Baratheon** | Cersei and Jaime's son, believed to be Robert's heir. Abuses Sansa and orders Ned's death. Reigns S1–4; poisoned at his wedding to Margaery in S4E2 through Olenna and Littlefinger's conspiracy. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joffrey_Baratheon) |
| **Tommen Baratheon** | Joffrey's younger brother; Margaery's husband. King in S4–6, caught between Cersei, Margaery and the High Sparrow. Dies by suicide after Cersei destroys the Sept with Margaery inside. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommen_Baratheon) |
| **Myrcella Baratheon** | Sister of Joffrey and Tommen; Trystane's betrothed. Sent to Dorne in S2. In S5 she accepts Jaime as her father, then dies from Ellaria's poison. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myrcella_Baratheon) |
| **Kevan Lannister** | Tywin's brother and Lancel's father; military and administrative deputy. Later serves Tommen as Hand; killed in the Sept explosion in S6E10. |
| **Lancel Lannister** | Kevan's son; Robert's squire and Cersei's lover. Helps facilitate Robert's fatal hunt; later joins the Faith Militant. Dies attempting to reach the wildfire beneath the Sept in S6E10. |
| **Shae** | Tyrion's lover and Sansa's maid. S1–4: their hidden relationship deteriorates under danger and Tyrion's marriage. Testifies against Tyrion; he finds her in Tywin's bed and kills her during his escape. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrion_Lannister) |
| **Bronn** | Mercenary who saves Tyrion at his S1 trial; later fights and travels with Jaime. Helps defend Blackwater and rescues Jaime from Drogon. S8: bargains for Highgarden and ends as Lord of Highgarden and Master of Coin. [Source](https://gameofthrones.fandom.com/wiki/Bronn) |
| **Podrick Payne** | Tyrion's squire, then Brienne's. Saves Tyrion at Blackwater; learns under Brienne and fights at Winterfell. S8 finale: knight and member of Bran's Kingsguard. |
| **Sandor “the Hound” Clegane** | Gregor's abused younger brother. Serves Joffrey, protects Sansa, then accompanies Arya. S4: badly injured fighting Brienne. S6–8: returns and fights the dead; persuades Arya to abandon revenge and dies killing Gregor. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandor_Clegane) |
| **Gregor “the Mountain” Clegane** | Tywin's brutal enforcer and Sandor's brother. Kills Oberyn but is mortally poisoned in S4; Qyburn transforms him into Cersei's silent protector. S8E5: kills Qyburn and dies fighting Sandor. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregor_Clegane) |
| **Brienne of Tarth** | Devoted to Renly, then Catelyn and her daughters; loves Jaime; mentors Podrick. Escorts Jaime, defeats the Hound, executes Stannis and protects Sansa. Knighted by Jaime in S8; ends as Lord Commander of Bran's Kingsguard. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brienne_of_Tarth) |

The Sept deaths are shown in [“The Winds of Winter”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Winds_of_Winter_(Game_of_Thrones)); Podrick's rescue and later position are covered by [“Blackwater”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackwater_(Game_of_Thrones)) and [“The Iron Throne”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Iron_Throne_(Game_of_Thrones)).

## 4. Baratheons, royal claimants and religious power

| Character | Relationships, highlights and timeline |
|---|---|
| **Robert Baratheon** | Ned's friend; Cersei's husband; once betrothed to Lyanna. Won the throne through rebellion. S1: brings Ned south and dies from a hunting injury after being plied with wine. His death opens the succession crisis. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Baratheon) |
| **Stannis Baratheon** | Robert's next brother; Selyse's husband and Shireen's father; served by Davos and Melisandre. S2: Renly's death strengthens his claim, but Blackwater defeats him. S4: saves the Watch. S5: sacrifices Shireen, loses to the Boltons and is executed by Brienne. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stannis_Baratheon) |
| **Renly Baratheon** | Youngest brother; Margaery's husband and Loras's lover. Claims the crown with Tyrell support. S2E5: killed by the supernatural shadow born from Melisandre and Stannis. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renly_Baratheon) |
| **Davos Seaworth** | Former smuggler, Stannis's adviser and Shireen's friend. Loses son Matthos at Blackwater; saves Gendry from sacrifice. After Stannis's fall he supports Jon and helps seek his resurrection. Survives to become Bran's Master of Ships. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davos_Seaworth) |
| **Melisandre** | Red priestess who first believes Stannis is her prophesied champion. S2: produces Renly's assassin; S5: promotes Shireen's sacrifice; S6: resurrects Jon. S8E3: lights defenses and guides Arya; removes her magical necklace and dies after victory. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melisandre) |
| **Selyse Baratheon** | Stannis's wife and Melisandre's devotee. Initially supports Shireen's sacrifice, then desperately objects; dies by suicide afterward in S5. |
| **Shireen Baratheon** | Stannis and Selyse's daughter; survived greyscale and teaches Davos to read. Burned alive by her parents' faction in S5E9 in an attempt to change Stannis's fortunes. |
| **Gendry** | Robert's unacknowledged son; smith and Arya's friend, later lover. S1–3: hunted for his parentage, sold to Melisandre and rescued by Davos. Returns S7; S8: makes weapons against the dead and is legitimized as Lord of Storm's End. |
| **High Sparrow** | Religious leader elevated by Cersei's political maneuvering in S5. Imprisons Cersei, Margaery and Loras; gains influence over Tommen. Killed with his congregation in S6E10. |
| **Septa Unella** | Enforces the Faith's punishment of Cersei and Margaery, including Cersei's walk. S6: Cersei imprisons her and leaves her with Gregor; exact subsequent fate is not shown. |

Shireen's sacrifice is in [“The Dance of Dragons”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dance_of_Dragons), the immediate consequences in [“Mother's Mercy”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother%27s_Mercy), and the Faith's destruction in [“The Winds of Winter”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Winds_of_Winter_(Game_of_Thrones)). Gendry's final elevation is in [“The Last of the Starks”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_of_the_Starks).

## 5. Daenerys and her inner circle

| Character | Relationships, highlights and timeline |
|---|---|
| **Daenerys Targaryen** | Aerys's daughter, sister to Rhaegar and Viserys; Drogo's widow and Jon's aunt/lover. S1: survives her brother and hatches dragons. S2–6: crosses Essos, frees enslaved people and rules Meereen. S7: invades Westeros. S8: fights the dead, destroys surrendered King's Landing and is killed by Jon. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daenerys_Targaryen) |
| **Viserys Targaryen** | Daenerys's abusive elder brother; trades her marriage for a promised army. S1E6: threatens her and her unborn child; Drogo kills him with molten gold. |
| **Khal Drogo** | Dothraki leader and Daenerys's husband. Their relationship begins coercively and later becomes affectionate. S1: kills Viserys; a wound and blood-magic intervention leave him unresponsive; Daenerys ends his life. Appears in her S2 vision. |
| **Jorah Mormont** | Jeor's exiled son; secretly spies on Daenerys before becoming devoted to her. Exposure leads to exile in S4. Contracts greyscale, is cured by Sam in S7 and returns. Dies defending Daenerys at Winterfell in S8E3. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorah_Mormont) |
| **Barristan Selmy** | Celebrated Kingsguard commander dismissed by Joffrey in S1. Joins Daenerys in S3 and offers memories of her family. Dies fighting Sons of the Harpy in Meereen in S5. |
| **Missandei** | Freed translator from Naath; Daenerys's trusted adviser and Grey Worm's partner. S3–8: accompanies Daenerys from Astapor to Westeros. Captured by Euron and executed by Gregor on Cersei's orders in S8E4. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missandei) |
| **Grey Worm** | Elected commander of the freed Unsullied; loves Missandei. S3–8: leads Daenerys's infantry in Essos and Westeros. After Missandei's death participates in the sack and executions; ultimately sails for Naath. [Source](https://gameofthrones.fandom.com/wiki/Grey_Worm) |
| **Daario Naharis** | Mercenary who kills his fellow commanders and joins Daenerys in S3; becomes her lover. Helps take cities and find her after her flight. S6: ordered to remain in Meereen with the Second Sons; later fate unshown. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daario_Naharis) |
| **Varys** | Spymaster, political rival of Littlefinger and later Tyrion's ally. Helps Tyrion escape in S4 and supports Daenerys. In S8 favors Jon's claim and plots against her; executed by Drogon. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varys) |
| **Illyrio Mopatis** | Wealthy Pentoshi patron sheltering Viserys and Daenerys in S1; helps arrange her marriage and gives the dragon eggs. Associates with Varys; no later on-screen resolution. |
| **Mirri Maz Duur** | Healer from a community attacked by Drogo's people. Her S1 magic leaves Drogo incapacitated and Daenerys's baby dead; Daenerys burns her on the funeral pyre from which the dragons hatch. |

For the early Targaryen turning points see [“A Golden Crown”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Golden_Crown) and [Season 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_1). Barristan's final arc is in [Season 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_5).

## 6. The Watch, the Free Folk and supernatural figures

| Character | Relationships, highlights and timeline |
|---|---|
| **Samwell Tarly** | Jon's closest friend; Gilly's partner; estranged son of Randyll. S1–3: joins the Watch and kills a White Walker with dragonglass. S5–7: helps elect Jon, studies at the Citadel and cures Jorah. Helps establish Jon's lineage; S8 ends as Grand Maester. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samwell_Tarly) |
| **Gilly** | Craster's daughter and victim of his incest; mother of Little Sam. Escapes with Sam in S3; travels south and discovers the record of Rhaegar's annulment while reading. S8: survives Winterfell and is pregnant with Sam's child. [Source](https://gameofthrones.fandom.com/wiki/Gilly) |
| **Little Sam** | Gilly and Craster's child, named after his protector Samwell. Born S3; rescued from sacrifice. Accompanies Gilly through the Watch, Horn Hill, Oldtown and Winterfell; survives. |
| **Jeor Mormont** | Jorah's father and Lord Commander. Mentors Jon and gives him Longclaw. Leads the Great Ranging; murdered during the S3 mutiny at Craster's Keep. |
| **Maester Aemon** | Elderly Targaryen who chose the Watch over dynastic power; mentor to Jon and Sam. Reveals his heritage in S1 and dies of old age in S5. |
| **Alliser Thorne** | Harsh Watch trainer and Jon's rival. Commands bravely at Castle Black in S4, but later leads the mutiny against Jon's wildling policy. Hanged by resurrected Jon in S6. |
| **Eddison “Dolorous Edd” Tollett** | Jon and Sam's friend. Survives northern expeditions, helps recover control after Jon's murder and succeeds him as commander. Dies saving Sam at Winterfell in S8E3. |
| **Ygritte** | Free Folk archer and Jon's lover. S2–3: captivity becomes romance; Jon's return to the Watch breaks their bond. S4E9: Olly shoots her during the Castle Black battle; she dies with Jon. |
| **Tormund Giantsbane** | Free Folk leader initially opposed to Jon, later his trusted ally. Survives Hardhome, the Bastards battle and Winterfell. S8: returns north with the surviving Free Folk; Jon joins their departure beyond the Wall. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tormund_Giantsbane) |
| **Mance Rayder** | Former Watchman who unites the Free Folk to escape the dead. S3–4: prepares and launches the attack on the Wall. S5E1: refuses submission to Stannis; Jon mercifully shoots him during his burning. |
| **Qhorin Halfhand** | Veteran ranger guiding Jon in S2. Engineers his own death at Jon's hands so the wildlings will accept Jon as a deserter. |
| **Craster** | Abusive wildling patriarch and unreliable Watch host. Sacrifices infant sons to the White Walkers. Killed by Karl Tanner during the S3 mutiny. |
| **Three-Eyed Raven** | Ancient visionary in a northern cave. Trains Bran in S6 after their S4 meeting. The Night King kills him; Bran takes his role. Do not assume every detail of the book character Bloodraven is confirmed on screen. |
| **Leaf** | Child of the Forest who aids Bran. S6 reveals the Children's creation of the first White Walker. Dies buying the group time during the cave attack. |
| **Night King** | Human transformed by the Children into the first White Walker. Raises the dead, kills the Raven, converts Viserion and breaches the Wall. Arya kills him in S8E3, destroying his supernatural army. Distinct from the books' legendary “Night's King.” [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_King) |
| **Beric Dondarrion** | Sent by Ned against Gregor; later Brotherhood leader repeatedly resurrected by Thoros. Allies with the Hound and Jon. Dies protecting Arya in S8E3, enabling her later attack on the Night King. |
| **Thoros of Myr** | Red priest, Beric's friend and source of his resurrections. S3: demonstrates resurrection to Arya. S7E6: injured by an undead bear and dies during the expedition beyond the Wall. |

The Watch's collapse at Craster's is in [“And Now His Watch Is Ended”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/And_Now_His_Watch_Is_Ended); the Wall battle in [“The Watchers on the Wall”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Watchers_on_the_Wall); Mance's death in [Season 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_5). The cave and resurrection stories are covered by [“The Door”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Door_(Game_of_Thrones)), [“Kissed by Fire”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kissed_by_Fire) and [“Beyond the Wall”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond_the_Wall_(Game_of_Thrones)).

## 7. Great houses, rivals and regional rulers

| Character | Relationships, highlights and timeline |
|---|---|
| **Petyr “Littlefinger” Baelish** | Loves Catelyn and later becomes obsessed with Sansa; manipulates Lysa. Helps engineer Jon Arryn's death, betrays Ned, conspires against Joffrey and gains the Vale. His schemes fail when the Stark siblings unite; Arya executes him on Sansa's judgment in S7E7. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petyr_Baelish) |
| **Lysa Arryn** | Catelyn's sister; Jon Arryn's widow and Robin's mother. Her poisoning of Jon at Littlefinger's urging starts the central conspiracy. Marries Littlefinger in S4; he pushes her through the Moon Door. |
| **Robin Arryn** | Lysa and Jon's son; nephew of Catelyn. S1 onward: sheltered young lord. Littlefinger exploits his authority; Royce trains him. Appears at the S8 council that selects Bran. |
| **Edmure Tully** | Catelyn and Lysa's brother; Roslin Frey's husband. S3: wedding becomes the Red Wedding and he is imprisoned. S6: compelled to surrender Riverrun. S8: alive at the final council. |
| **Brynden “Blackfish” Tully** | Uncle to Catelyn, Lysa and Edmure. Escapes the Red Wedding, retakes Riverrun and refuses to abandon it. Reported killed fighting after its S6 surrender. |
| **Walder Frey** | Lord controlling the Twins crossing. Robb's broken marriage pledge becomes a pretext for his Lannister–Bolton alliance and the Red Wedding. Arya kills him in S6E10 and uses his face to poison participating Frey men in S7E1. |
| **Roose Bolton** | Robb's commander; Ramsay's father. Betrays and personally kills Robb at the Red Wedding, becoming northern ruler under the crown. Ramsay murders him in S6E2. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roose_Bolton) |
| **Ramsay Bolton / Snow** | Roose's legitimized son; tortures Theon into “Reek” and marries and abuses Sansa. Murders his father and threatens the remaining Starks. Defeated in S6E9; Sansa releases his own hounds on him. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramsay_Bolton) |
| **Theon Greyjoy** | Balon's son and Yara's brother; raised with the Starks. S2: betrays Robb and captures Winterfell. S3–5: tortured by Ramsay, then saves Sansa. S8: rescues Yara and dies defending Bran from the Night King. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theon_Greyjoy) |
| **Yara Greyjoy** | Theon's sister and an experienced captain. Attempts to rescue him, loses the kingsmoot to Euron and allies with Daenerys. Captured S7, freed S8; retakes the Iron Islands and attends the final council. |
| **Balon Greyjoy** | Father to Yara and Theon. Rejects Robb's alliance and invades the North in S2. His brother Euron kills him in S6. |
| **Euron Greyjoy** | Uncle to Yara and Theon; murders Balon and wins the kingsmoot. Allies with Cersei, destroys enemy fleets and kills Rhaegal. Jaime mortally wounds him in S8E5. |
| **Aeron Greyjoy** | Brother of Balon and Euron; priest of the Drowned God. S6: oversees Balon's funeral and the kingsmoot. Later on-screen fate unspecified. [Source](https://gameofthrones.fandom.com/wiki/Aeron_Greyjoy) |
| **Margaery Tyrell** | Loras's sister and Olenna's granddaughter. Marries Renly, Joffrey and Tommen; uses charm, charity and political intelligence. Imprisoned by the Faith in S5; recognizes the danger at the Sept too late in S6 and dies. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaery_Tyrell) |
| **Olenna Tyrell** | Mace's mother and Margaery/Loras's grandmother. Helps poison Joffrey to protect Margaery. After her family's destruction supports Daenerys; takes Jaime's poison after Highgarden falls in S7, then confesses Joffrey's murder. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olenna_Tyrell) |
| **Loras Tyrell** | Margaery's brother and Renly's lover; celebrated knight. Helps secure the Lannister–Tyrell alliance. Arrested by the Faith; dies in the S6 Sept explosion. |
| **Mace Tyrell** | Olenna's son; father to Margaery and Loras; royal councillor. Travels to the Iron Bank and is killed at the Sept in S6. |
| **Oberyn Martell** | Doran and Elia's brother, Ellaria's lover, father of the Sand Snakes. S4: seeks justice for Elia; represents Tyrion in trial by combat. Gregor kills him, though Oberyn's poison nearly kills Gregor. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberyn_Martell) |
| **Ellaria Sand** | Oberyn's partner and Tyene's mother. S5: poisons Myrcella for revenge. S6: overthrows Doran. S7: captured and chained opposite poisoned Tyene; the show does not depict her ultimate death. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellaria_Sand) |
| **Doran Martell** | Oberyn's older brother and Trystane's father; favors restraint toward the Lannisters. Ellaria murders him during the S6 coup. |
| **Trystane Martell** | Doran's son and Myrcella's loving betrothed. Appears S5–6; Obara kills him aboard a ship in S6E1. [Source](https://gameofthrones.fandom.com/wiki/Trystane_Martell) |
| **Obara Sand** | Oberyn's spear-fighting daughter; supports Ellaria and murders Trystane. Euron kills her in S7E2. |
| **Nymeria Sand** | Oberyn's daughter, a whip fighter and Obara/Tyene's half-sister. Participates in Ellaria's faction; Euron kills her in S7E2. |
| **Tyene Sand** | Daughter of Oberyn and Ellaria; poisons Bronn then saves him; kills Areo during the coup. Cersei poisons her in S7E3 and forces Ellaria to watch her dying. |

The Riverlands outcomes appear in [“No One”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_One_(Game_of_Thrones)); the Greyjoy and Dornish reversals in [“Home”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_(Game_of_Thrones)), [“The Red Woman”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Red_Woman), [“Stormborn”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stormborn) and [“The Queen's Justice”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Queen%27s_Justice). Yara's final position is shown in [Season 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_8).

|---|---|

| Gerold Hightower | Fellow Kingsguard at the Tower of Joy, killed during the same flashback fight. |

| Rickard Stark | Father of Ned, Lyanna, Benjen and Brandon; seen in a S6 vision. Aerys killed him before the series. |

| Viserion | Pale dragon named for Viserys. Night King kills and reanimates him in S7; breaches the Wall. Destroyed with the Night King's forces in S8. |
| Ghost | Jon's white direwolf. Survives the wars and rejoins Jon beyond the Wall in the finale. |
| Grey Wind | Robb's direwolf and battlefield companion. Killed at the Red Wedding. |
| Lady | Sansa's direwolf. Ned reluctantly kills her in S1 after Cersei demands punishment for Nymeria's attack on Joffrey. |
| Nymeria | Arya's direwolf. Driven away for protection in S1; found leading a wolf pack in S7 and remains wild. |
| Summer | Bran's direwolf. Saves him from an assassin; dies protecting the cave escape in S6. |
| Shaggydog | Rickon's direwolf. Killed by the Umbers before they deliver Rickon to Ramsay in S6. |
| Ser Pounce | Tommen's cat, seen in S4 during Margaery's courtship. Later fate not established on screen. |

The lineage revelations are in [“The Dragon and the Wolf”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dragon_and_the_Wolf); dragon deaths in [“Beyond the Wall”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond_the_Wall_(Game_of_Thrones)) and [“The Last of the Starks”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_of_the_Starks). The wolves' stories intersect with [Arya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arya_Stark), [Bran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bran_Stark), [Robb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robb_Stark) and [Rickon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rickon_Stark).

Important people **mentioned but not given ordinary on-screen character arcs** include Elia Martell and her murdered children, Joanna Lannister, Rhaella Targaryen, Ned's elder brother Brandon Stark, Jon's supposed mother Wylla, Tyrion's first wife Tysha, and historical rulers such as Aegon the Conqueror. These people explain motivations but should not be confused with living members of the show's cast. Similarly, Lady Stoneheart, Young Griff, Arianne Martell and Victarion Greyjoy do not receive their book storylines in this series.

## 13. Major events in chronological order

### Before Season 1

- The Children of the Forest create the first White Walker as a weapon against humans; their creation eventually threatens them too.
- Robert's Rebellion ends Targaryen rule. Robert kills Rhaegar at the Trident; Tywin's forces sack King's Landing; Jaime kills Aerys. Elia and her children are murdered.
- At the Tower of Joy, Ned discovers Lyanna's newborn son and conceals Jon's identity to protect him.
- Balon's earlier rebellion fails; Theon becomes Ned's ward/hostage.
- Lysa poisons Jon Arryn at Littlefinger's urging, then falsely implicates the Lannisters, drawing Ned toward the capital.

These are backstory and later revelations, not a continuous prequel depicted on screen. See [Ned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ned_Stark), [Robert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Baratheon), [Littlefinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petyr_Baelish) and the [Night King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_King).

### Season 1 — The succession crisis

White Walkers reappear; Robert visits Winterfell; Jaime pushes Bran. Ned becomes Hand and investigates the royal children's parentage. Catelyn arrests Tyrion, escalating Stark–Lannister violence. Robert dies; Littlefinger betrays Ned. Robb takes the field. Joffrey executes Ned in E9; northern lords acclaim Robb as king. Across the sea, Viserys, Drogo and Daenerys's baby die; her dragons hatch in E10. [Season 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_1)

### Season 2 — The War of the Five Kings

The five claimants are Joffrey, Stannis, Renly, Robb and Balon; not all seek the same territory. Renly is assassinated. Theon takes Winterfell; Bran and Rickon escape. Arya survives Harrenhal with Jaqen's help. Jon infiltrates the Free Folk. Daenerys survives betrayal in Qarth. Stannis loses at Blackwater, strengthening the Lannister–Tyrell coalition. The dead advance on the Watch's northern expedition. [Season 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_2)

### Season 3 — Liberation and betrayal

Daenerys frees the Unsullied and takes Yunkai. Jon and Ygritte become lovers; he eventually rejoins the Watch. The mutiny at Craster's kills Jeor. Jaime loses his hand and confides in Brienne. Ramsay destroys Theon's identity. Robb executes Karstark and loses allies. The Red Wedding in E9 murders Robb, Catelyn, Talisa and many followers, breaking the northern war effort. [Season 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_3)

### Season 4 — The old balance collapses

Joffrey dies at the Purple Wedding. Sansa escapes; Littlefinger murders Lysa. Tyrion's trial ends with Oberyn's death; Tyrion escapes after killing Shae and Tywin. Daenerys takes Meereen but struggles to govern. The Watch defeats the assault on Castle Black; Stannis defeats Mance's remaining host. Bran reaches the Raven; Arya leaves for Braavos. [Season 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_4)

### Season 5 — Rule becomes harder than conquest

Jon becomes Lord Commander and makes peace with the Free Folk; Hardhome shows the scale of the dead. The Faith imprisons Margaery and Cersei, culminating in Cersei's walk of atonement. Sansa marries Ramsay and escapes with Theon. Stannis sacrifices Shireen and loses his army. Daenerys escapes the pit attack on Drogon. Myrcella is poisoned; Jon's men murder him. [Season 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_5)

### Season 6 — The survivors regain power

Jon is resurrected. Ramsay murders Roose; Ellaria overthrows Doran; Euron kills Balon. Bran learns the Walkers' origin and Hodor's tragedy. Daenerys burns the khals and defeats the masters at Meereen. Arya rejects the Faceless Men's identity and kills Walder. Jon and Sansa recover Winterfell. Cersei destroys the Sept, loses Tommen and takes the crown. Daenerys sails west. [Season 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_6)

### Season 7 — The wars converge

Daenerys lands at Dragonstone and meets Jon. Cersei's forces defeat several of her allies, but Daenerys devastates a Lannister column. The Stark siblings reunite and expose Littlefinger. Jon's expedition captures a wight at the cost of Viserion. Cersei falsely promises assistance. Jon's legitimate Targaryen birth is revealed as he and Daenerys become lovers. Undead Viserion breaks the Wall. [Season 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_7)

### Season 8 — Victory, massacre and a new settlement

Jon learns his parentage. Jaime knights Brienne. Arya kills the Night King at Winterfell. Rhaegal and Missandei die; Daenerys executes Varys. King's Landing surrenders, but Daenerys burns it. Jaime and Cersei die together; both Cleganes die fighting. Jon kills Daenerys. Bran is elected king, Sansa secures northern independence, Arya sails west, and Jon returns north. [Season 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_8)

## 14. Battles, sieges and military turning points

“Reported” means the show provides news or aftermath rather than a full combat sequence. These entries cover the major military changes; small tavern fights and every unnamed raid are not separate wars.

| When | Conflict | Sides, outcome and consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Before S1 | Robert's Rebellion: Trident, sack of King's Landing, Tower of Joy | Rebel coalition defeats the Targaryen regime; Robert becomes king. The Tower encounter is a small fight protecting the secret of Jon's birth. |
| Before S1 | Greyjoy Rebellion | Robert's regime defeats Balon; Theon's removal to Winterfell establishes his divided loyalties. |
| S1E9 | Green Fork | Tywin defeats a northern diversion. Robb sacrifices the force to enable his real attack elsewhere. |
| S1E9 | Whispering Wood | Robb surprises Jaime's force and captures Jaime, gaining an important hostage. |
| S1 campaign, largely reported | Fighting around Riverrun | Stark–Tully successes loosen the Lannister grip on the Riverlands. |
| S2E4 aftermath | Oxcross | Robb defeats a Lannister force; he meets Talisa while the wounded are treated. |
| S2 | Ironborn invasion of the North | Balon's forces exploit Robb's southern campaign. Theon captures Winterfell; northern defenses and Stark authority collapse. |
| S2E10 aftermath | Sack of Winterfell | Ramsay's force takes the castle after Theon's men betray him. Winterfell is burned and Theon becomes a prisoner. |
| S2E9 | **Blackwater** | Stannis attacks King's Landing. Tyrion's wildfire and defense delay him; Tywin and Tyrell reinforcements win for Joffrey. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackwater_(Game_of_Thrones)) |
| S2E10–S3E1, largely off-screen | Fist of the First Men | The dead overwhelm the Watch's expedition, causing a disastrous retreat. |
| S3, reported | Stone Mill | Edmure wins a local engagement but disrupts Robb's intended larger strategy against Tywin. |
| S3E4 | Liberation of Astapor | Daenerys turns the Unsullied against the masters and frees them; gains her principal infantry force. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/And_Now_His_Watch_Is_Ended) |
| S3E9 | Taking of Yunkai | Daario, Jorah and Grey Worm lead an infiltration; the city's defenses collapse and enslaved residents are freed. |
| S4E4 | Taking of Meereen | Grey Worm helps arm an internal uprising; Daenerys wins the city and begins ruling it. |
| S4E5 | Raid on Craster's Keep | Jon destroys the Watch mutineers; Bran's group escapes without meeting him. |
| S4E6 | Yara's Dreadfort rescue attempt | Yara attacks to recover Theon; his trauma and Ramsay's resistance force her withdrawal. |
| S4E8 | Moat Cailin | Ramsay uses Theon to obtain the ironborn garrison's surrender, then has the surrendered men killed. |
| S4E9 | **Castle Black / battle for the Wall** | The Watch repels attacks from both sides. Ygritte, Pyp and Grenn die. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Watchers_on_the_Wall) |
| S4E10 | Stannis attacks Mance's camp | Stannis's cavalry defeats and captures Mance, breaking the immediate wildling offensive. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Children_(Game_of_Thrones)) |
| S5E8 | **Hardhome** | A rescue negotiation becomes a battle against the dead. Jon kills a Walker with Longclaw; some refugees escape, but the dead overrun the settlement. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardhome) |
| S5E9 | Daznak's Pit attack | Harpy insurgents attack Daenerys's gathering. Drogon returns; Daenerys escapes on his back. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dance_of_Dragons) |
| S5E10 | Stannis's defeat outside Winterfell | Bolton cavalry routs Stannis's depleted army. Brienne finds and executes him afterward. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother%27s_Mercy) |
| S6E7–8 | Siege of Riverrun | Jaime forces Edmure to order surrender; the Blackfish dies resisting. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_One_(Game_of_Thrones)) |
| S6E8–9 | **Masters' siege of Meereen** | Daenerys's dragons destroy enemy ships; her Dothraki attack the Harpies. The masters submit. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Bastards) |
| S6E9 | **Battle of the Bastards** | Ramsay kills Rickon and nearly traps Jon's army. Knights of the Vale, summoned through Sansa, turn the battle; Winterfell returns to the Starks. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Bastards) |
| S7E2 | Euron's attack on Yara's fleet | Euron captures Yara and Ellaria, kills Obara and Nymeria, and disrupts Daenerys's Dornish alliance. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stormborn) |
| S7E3 | Casterly Rock and Highgarden | Unsullied capture a deliberately weakened Rock but lose their ships; Jaime instead seizes Highgarden and its wealth. Olenna dies. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Queen%27s_Justice) |
| S7E4 | **Goldroad / Loot Train attack** | Daenerys, Drogon and Dothraki devastate Jaime's returning army and supplies. Bronn saves Jaime; the Tarlys are executed afterward in E5. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Spoils_of_War_(Game_of_Thrones)) |
| S7E6 | **Wight hunt beyond the Wall** | Jon's party captures a wight but becomes trapped. Daenerys rescues survivors; Thoros, Viserion and Benjen die during the mission. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond_the_Wall_(Game_of_Thrones)) |
| S7E7 | Breach of the Wall | The Night King uses undead Viserion to destroy Eastwatch's section, opening the route south. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dragon_and_the_Wolf) |
| S8E1 aftermath | Last Hearth | The dead destroy House Umber's seat; Ned Umber's reanimated body becomes their warning. |
| S8E3 | **Winterfell / the Long Night** | Allied living armies nearly fall; Arya kills the Night King, ending his army. Jorah, Theon, Lyanna, Edd and Beric die; Melisandre dies after victory. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Long_Night_(Game_of_Thrones)) |
| S8E4 | Ambush near Dragonstone | Euron's fleet kills Rhaegal, destroys ships and captures Missandei, whose execution follows. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_of_the_Starks) |
| S8E5 | **King's Landing / the Bells** | Drogon destroys the fleet and defenses. The city surrenders; Daenerys nevertheless burns it and her troops massacre inhabitants. Cersei's regime ends. [Episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bells_(Game_of_Thrones)) |

Early campaigns are cross-referenced in the episode summaries for [Season 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_1), [Season 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_2), [Season 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_3) and [Season 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_season_4).

### Major killings and duels that are not army battles

- **Ned's execution — S1E9:** destroys the possibility of a negotiated Stark submission.
- **Renly's assassination — S2E5:** supernatural killing reallocates his army and Tyrell support.
- **Red Wedding — S3E9:** planned massacre under guest protection, not an ordinary battlefield defeat.
- **Purple Wedding — S4E2:** Joffrey's poisoning; triggers Tyrion's prosecution.
- **Oberyn versus Gregor — S4E8:** trial by combat; Oberyn's death condemns Tyrion despite Gregor's poisoning.
- **Brienne versus Sandor — S4E10:** both claim to protect Arya; she chooses her own escape.
- **Shireen's burning — S5E9:** sacrifice ordered by her own faction, not an enemy execution.
- **Great Sept explosion — S6E10:** Cersei's mass killing removes the Tyrell leadership and Faith leadership.
- **Frey revenge — S6E10/S7E1:** Arya kills Walder and later poisons men gathered under his identity.
- **Littlefinger's execution — S7E7:** the Stark siblings defeat his effort to divide them.
- **Clegane duel — S8E5:** Sandor sacrifices himself to kill Gregor amid the city's destruction.
- **Daenerys's assassination — S8E6:** Jon ends her rule; Drogon destroys the throne, and the lords arrange a new monarchy.

These turning points are detailed in [“The Rains of Castamere”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rains_of_Castamere), [“The Lion and the Rose”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lion_and_the_Rose), [“The Mountain and the Viper”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mountain_and_the_Viper), [“The Children”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Children_(Game_of_Thrones)), [“The Winds of Winter”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Winds_of_Winter_(Game_of_Thrones)) and [“The Iron Throne”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Iron_Throne_(Game_of_Thrones)).

## 15. Where the principal survivors finish

Bran rules six kingdoms; Sansa rules an independent North. Tyrion is Hand, Brienne leads the Kingsguard, Podrick joins it, Sam is Grand Maester, Davos is Master of Ships and Bronn is Master of Coin and Lord of Highgarden. Gendry holds Storm's End, Yara the Iron Islands, Robin the Vale and Edmure his restored position. Arya sails west. Grey Worm sets sail for Naath. Jon, sentenced to the Watch, is last seen travelling beyond the Wall with Tormund, Ghost and the Free Folk; the show does **not** explicitly crown him their king. [Finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Iron_Throne_(Game_of_Thrones))

Several absences are deliberately left unresolved here: the precise later lives of Meera, Daario, Hot Pie, Quaithe, Syrio, Ilyn Payne and many minor figures are not fully shown. Ellaria and Unella are left in horrific captivity, but their ultimate deaths are not filmed. Survival until a last appearance is not proof of survival through every subsequent event.
